target_customer: Small and medium businesses in Nigeria needing short-term working capital loans
problem: Nigerian SMEs have little access to fast credit from banks; Payhippo promised loans in under 3 hours using its own scoring on SME data.
business_model: Digital lender: interest and fees on short-term SME loans, later a microfinance bank acquisition and a pivot to clean energy financing
product_category: SME digital lending, later clean energy financing

founders.name: Zach Bijesse
previous_startups: Mobile health app started at the end of college (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no university or employers. Taught in Manhattan and worked as a certified weight loss specialist per his own YC bio.

founders.name: Chioma Okotcha
founders.background_notes: YC bio mentions policy analysis; later reported as COO of Rivy.

founders.name: Uche Nnadi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCabal coverage of the Maritime MFB deal, not on the YC page; background not found.

competitors.name: Carbon (formerly Paylater)
competitors.what: Nigerian digital lender offering fast loans
competitors.traction_then: Named among Nigerian digital lenders in 2019 coverage

competitors.name: FairMoney
competitors.what: Nigerian digital lender, personal loans first, later SME
competitors.traction_then: Named among Nigerian digital lenders in 2019 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile loan origination plus an in-house credit scoring model on SME data; standard fintech engineering, with the hard part being underwriting quality rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data could improve scoring but lenders in Nigeria were many and capital was the real constraint; no licence moat until the pending bank acquisition.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it. The company pivoted itself in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCabal 2021 coverage cited over 40 million SMEs in Nigeria and Payhippo reported 5,000 loans disbursed worth about $1 million with a 97 percent repayment rate and $64,000 in revenue before the seed round.

identity.mascot_or_character: Hippo implied by the name; one profile says the founders call themselves Hippos

rebrands.why: Shift from SME lending to clean energy financing, per TechMoran and Techpoint in March 2025

brand_strength.rationale: Only funding and rebrand coverage was found, with no press on the brand itself; the pay prefix no longer fit after the energy pivot.

pivots.to: Clean energy financing as Rivy (solar inventory financing, asset financing, micro-grids, carbon finance)
pivots.why: Techpoint cites the complexity of SME lending in Nigeria and the growth of African climate tech funding

outcome_analysis: Payhippo raised a 1 million dollar pre-seed and a 3 million dollar seed in 2021 from African fintech founders and bought a microfinance bank in 2022 pending central bank approval. Public sources show no shutdown, but in March 2025 it rebranded as Rivy and moved from SME lending to clean energy financing, citing the difficulty of SME lending. The company is active, and whether the pivot succeeds is not yet known.
notes: The company site payhippo.africa could not be fetched (host not resolvable in this session), so it is treated as unreachable, likely due to the rebrand. The March 2025 four million dollar figure comes from Techpoint and TechMoran; Techpoint says it includes a 2 million dollar equity round co-led by EchoVC and All-On plus local debt, and TechMoran says nothing about a pre-Series A label while an All-On release headline does, so stage is other. The 2021 seed lead differs by outlet: several name Chipper Cash founders, one names Hakeem Belo-Osagie. Maritime Microfinance Bank acquisition (Nov 2022) approval status unknown. Competitor sources are dated 2019 and describe personal lenders; no SME-specific rival source dated near mid 2021 was found. Uche Nnadi and Okotcha roles from TechCabal and secondary summaries.
